stakeholders.name: Individual members
stakeholders.role: Freelancers and regulars who pay the full rate
stakeholders.stake: Belonging, recognition, and a real say in how the space changes

stakeholders.name: Anchor organisations
stakeholders.stake: Stable, affordable space that carries them through the winter

evidence.note: Discussed as a category. No one in the room spoke as an anchor organisation.

stakeholders.name: Staff and programme team
stakeholders.role: They run the calendar, the café and the welcome
stakeholders.stake: A programme they can sustain without burning out

stakeholders.name: The board
stakeholders.role: Holds the accounts and the contracts
stakeholders.stake: Decisions that get made and hold, without losing the membership

evidence.note: Talked about in the third person all day and never heard from directly.

stakeholders.name: Neighbours and the street
stakeholders.role: The public on the ground floor's doorstep
stakeholders.stake: A building they can walk into

evidence.note: The ground-floor argument is about their doorstep. Members argued both sides of it in their name.

stakeholders.name: Funders
stakeholders.role: Grant-makers whose money comes with reporting conditions

evidence.note: Has the most structural power over the outcome and appears in the room only as grant conditions.

relations.label: the subsidy nobody chose
relations.detail: Full-rate members cover the discounted rooms the anchor organisations hold. The discounts predate most of the current membership, and nobody at the money table knew who set them.

aspects.note: Neither group can change the rates. The tiers sit in contracts the board signed years ago.
Full-rate members said the subsidy makes them question renewing.

relations.label: gatekeeper, coach, or infrastructure
relations.detail: The programme team curates what happens in the building. Members describe their best experiences as unprogrammed and ask for permission and the keys instead.

aspects.note: Members offering to host is unused capacity for a team that says it is stretched.

relations.label: openness versus quiet
relations.detail: The ground floor is the only part of the building a non-member can reach, and the only part the quiet-paying members cannot avoid.

aspects.note: Members who pay for quiet said opening the doors would remove the one thing they cannot get anywhere else.

relations.label: decisions fall between meetings
relations.detail: Members and the board meet twice a year. The decisions too big for consensus wait for those meetings, and often past them.

aspects.note: Members defer upward, the board defers back to consensus, and nobody ends up holding the big decisions.

relations.label: the reports land on staff
relations.detail: Staff write the reports the grants require. The programme manager now spends more time reporting than programming.

aspects.note: Staff carry the funders' conditions without ever meeting the funders.

relations.label: grants with conditions attached
relations.detail: The anchor organisations' bookings are paid from grants, and each grant's reporting conditions shape what they can commit to here.

aspects.note: The funders set the conditions; the organisations can meet them or lose the money.

relations.label: answers for the money
relations.detail: The board answers to funders for how the money is spent.

aspects.note: Every pound arrives with conditions the board did not set.

relations.label: delegates the day-to-day
relations.detail: The board delegates the running of the building to staff and mostly stays out of it.

aspects.note: The board knows the accounts and staff know the building. The two halves rarely meet.

relations.label: block bookings anchor the calendar
relations.detail: The anchor organisations' regular bookings are the fixed points the staff build the calendar around, and the steadiest income they can plan on.

relations.label: the café faces the street
relations.detail: The café is the one place a neighbour can already walk into, and the staff run it.

aspects.note: Opening the ground floor would extend something the café already does, rather than start something new.
